Caitlin Rourk

Democratic candidate for U.S. Representative, District 10, Travis County, Texas · Open seat

U.S. Army Reserve officer and communications professional (formerly in corporate communications at Dell Technologies)

Caitlin Rourk is the Democratic nominee for Texas' 10th Congressional District. The seat is open because Rep. Michael McCaul, who has held it since 2005, is not running for reelection. She has never held elected office, and she faces Republican Chris Gober in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Rourk stands

Economy and rural communities
Says she will be pro-growth and pro-community: welcoming investment while protecting the public interest, so that residents, not only large donors, have a seat at the table as TX-10 grows.
Economy and rural communities
Held a listening session in Navasota on data centers and large industrial projects. Says constituents should be heard before decisions that affect local water, power, and infrastructure.
Border security
Lists securing the border and fixing the immigration system among the projects she says Congress should focus on for Texas's future.
Free speech and elections
Lists reducing corruption and dark money in politics as a top priority. Calls for more transparency about who influences government, and her campaign does not accept corporate PAC money.
Health care
Proposes lowering drug costs, protecting coverage for pre-existing conditions, ending surprise billing, expanding mental health services, strengthening the ACA, and advocating for Medicaid expansion.
Foreign policy and military
Supports keeping America safe without what she calls endless, costly wars. Says any use of military force should have a clear strategy for success.
Education
Lists strong public schools and investment in public education among her top priorities.

Background

  • Democratic nominee, U.S. House Texas District 10 (2026)
  • Earlier filed in Texas' 31st Congressional District race and did not appear on that ballot (2026)
  • Enlisted in the Texas Army National Guard at age 28, then commissioned through Army Officer Candidate School; served in military intelligence and public affairs
  • Supported the Texas Military Department's responses to Hurricane Harvey, COVID-19, and border mobilizations; later moved to the U.S. Army Reserve
  • Worked in public policy in Washington and in corporate communications at Dell Technologies
  • B.A. in political science, University of Chicago
  • MBA, University of Texas at Austin McCombs School of Business
  • Has never held elected office
